research_method.claude: MLR: SLR (Kitchenham) in ACM DL, IEEE Xplore and Scopus (815 records, 6 included + 5 via snowballing = 11) plus grey literature review of Dev.to (Garousi et al.; Strategy A 100 posts -> 9, Strategy B 59 posts -> 6); GQM, PICO; thematic synthesis (Cruzes & Dyba), 24 + 23 themes
research_method.nlm: MLR: SLR (Kitchenham) with snowballing (6 + 5 = 11 studies) plus Dev.to grey literature (Garousi et al.; 9 + 6 = 15 posts); GQM, PICO, quasi-gold standard; thematic synthesis, 24 + 23 themes
research_method.value: Multivocal literature review: SLR (Kitchenham guidelines) in ACM DL, IEEE Xplore and Scopus with backward/forward snowballing (6 + 5 = 11 studies) plus grey literature review of Dev.to posts (Garousi et al.; two search strategies, 9 + 6 = 15 posts); GQM goal, PICO strings, quasi-gold standard; thematic synthesis (Cruzes & Dyba) yielding 24 SLR and 23 GLR themes
research_method.note: Record counts (815 returned; 100 and 59 posts screened) given only by Claude, not contradicted.

context.claude: Mixed (academic studies on software professionals and LGBTQIA+ practitioner posts); 11 studies + 15 posts
context.nlm: Industry and online developer community (Dev.to), agile software engineering; 26 sources (11 academic, 15 grey)
context.value: academic (secondary/review); 26 sources (11 academic studies and 15 Dev.to practitioner posts) on LGBTQIA+ developers in agile teams

dora_applied.note: Both state DORA is not cited.

space_applied.note: Both state SPACE is not cited.

remote_covid.note: Remote/hybrid work as a safety and identity-control mechanism is a synthesized finding and a recommendation (not the study's own setting).

data_window.note: Review coverage period not stated by either.

cat_productivity.note: Claude lists diverse vs. non-diverse team productivity (reported by S1) as a Productivity metric; NotebookLM mentions higher productivity of diverse teams only as a finding, with no productivity metric. Thin basis.

cat_collaboration.note: Psychological safety, team dynamics and inclusion; destructive criticism in code reviews.

cat_satisfaction.note: Affect dimension of DX (Fagerholm & Münch), engagement, frustration, belonging, impostor syndrome.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM tags retention/turnover risk 'Delivery / DevEx', which is not a delivery metric.

cat_devex.note: DX lens is Fagerholm & Münch (cognition, conation, affect); Greiler/Storey/Noda actionable framework only referenced.

cat_agile.note: Agile teams are the setting (search string includes scrum, XP, squads), but no process metric is synthesized.

cat_survey.note: NotebookLM lists questionnaires, interviews and psychological-safety scales as collection for DX dimensions. Claude: industry satisfaction/productivity surveys only cited in background; the review synthesizes perceptions from qualitative studies and posts.

evidence.quote: This study aimed to examine traditional and grey literature data through a Multivocal Literature Review focused on the DX of LGBTQIA+ professionals in agile teams.
Stage 3) We classified the studies and updated the systematic review employing backward and forward snowballing. Then, we conducted a thematic synthesis of all included studies.
Table III lists all the works included in the mapping of traditional literature (six studies)
In Strategy A, nine documents (posts) were included, in Strategy B, six documents were included.
The studies recommend offering remote or hybrid work options, promoting democratic structures that allow workspace choice, and fostering inclusive recruitment and onboarding (S2, S9, S10).
In remote work (S2), LGBTQIA+ professionals benefit from a sense of safety and control, which aids team integration and performance, though challenges like isolation and invisibility persist.
This dynamic supports agile environments by fostering psychological safety while highlighting areas for improved visibility and inclusive communication.
This issue of invisibility in S2 relates to team integration and engagement, impacting developers' motivation in agile environments.
Conversely, professionals who feel welcomed by their teams and organizations, especially in processes tailored to their needs, report more positive team dynamics and engagement.
